objective: Make fault coverage aggregation refuse contradictory evidence instead of resolving it by iteration order: a fault claimed twice or claimed both SIMULATED and HARDWARE_TESTED is refused, a physical evidence reference recorded for a fault that is not HARDWARE_TESTED is refused, every entry carries exactly one status from the controlled vocabulary, and the top-level counts equal the number of entries in each status.
decision_supported: Given a set of caller-supplied coverage claims, does the report either state one honest status per fault backed by the evidence supplied for that fault, or refuse the input, rather than emitting a report whose per-fault status and top-level counts depend on argument order?
outputs: coverage_report() refuses a fault claimed twice, a fault claimed both SIMULATED and HARDWARE_TESTED, an undeclared fault name and a physical evidence reference attached to a fault that is not HARDWARE_TESTED.
coverage_report() emits physical_evidence_ref only on HARDWARE_TESTED entries and derives simulated_count, hardware_tested_count and not_executed_count from the emitted entries.

Tests covering duplicate membership, a simulated fault with a physical reference, a hardware plus simulated conflict, an orphan evidence key, count/entry consistency and a valid hardware-tested fixture with its reference.
acceptance: Refusal is chosen over documented precedence: coverage_report(simulated=[f], hardware_tested=[f]) raises FaultInjectionError naming the fault, in either argument order, and no status is written for it; asserted by tests/integration/test_fault_injection_coverage.py::test_coverage_refuses_a_fault_claimed_both_simulated_and_hardware_tested.

A repeated fault name in one claim raises FaultInjectionError instead of counting as a second unit of coverage; asserted by tests/integration/test_fault_injection_coverage.py::test_coverage_refuses_the_same_fault_claimed_twice.

A physical evidence reference for a fault that is not HARDWARE_TESTED raises FaultInjectionError, whether the fault is SIMULATED or NOT_EXECUTED, so the reference is refused rather than dropped; asserted by tests/integration/test_fault_injection_coverage.py::test_coverage_refuses_a_physical_reference_for_a_fault_that_is_not_hardware_tested.

Every emitted entry carries exactly one status from COVERAGE_STATUSES, only HARDWARE_TESTED entries carry a physical_evidence_ref and every other entry reports null; asserted by tests/integration/test_fault_injection_coverage.py::test_coverage_omits_a_physical_reference_for_every_non_hardware_entry.

simulated_count, hardware_tested_count and not_executed_count each equal the number of emitted entries in that status and sum to declared_count; asserted by tests/integration/test_fault_injection_coverage.py::test_coverage_counts_match_the_entries_in_each_status.

A valid evidence-only report with no simulated claims is accepted, marks each claimed fault HARDWARE_TESTED with its own reference and leaves the rest NOT_EXECUTED; asserted by tests/integration/test_fault_injection_coverage.py::test_a_valid_evidence_only_report_is_accepted.

Unknown, non-string and duplicate fault names still fail closed: non-string names raise FaultInjectionError rather than TypeError; asserted by tests/integration/test_fault_injection_coverage.py::test_coverage_refuses_an_undeclared_fault_name.

A report with no evidence still reports every declared fault NOT_EXECUTED and counts them; covered by tests/integration/test_fault_injection_coverage.py::test_coverage_never_reports_a_fault_as_passing_by_default.
The pre-existing hardware claim without a reference refusal and the JSON-serializable versioned document test still pass unchanged.
No injector, fault taxonomy, scenario manifest, runtime control path, interface schema or physical evidence claim is modified.

stop_conditions: The fix would mark a fault hardware-tested from a name alone, or invent, copy or upgrade a physical evidence reference.
The fix requires changing an injector, the fault taxonomy, a scenario manifest, an interface schema, libs/contracts or any path outside allowed_paths.
Meeting the acceptance requires a runtime, safety-MCU, dashboard or backend behavior change rather than a coverage-report change.
A contradictory input can only be handled by silently picking one claim, by last-write-wins, or by downgrading the fault to NOT_EXECUTED.
A targeted or required repository check fails for a reason caused by this diff and cannot be corrected inside allowed_paths.
data_classification: internal; the tests use declared fault names, synthetic evidence reference paths and no real robot, operator, camera or credential data
model_policy: no model call; coverage validation and counting are deterministic pure functions over caller-supplied claim lists
risks_and_fallbacks: Refusal versus precedence is a QA Owner decision this Packet depends on. Refusal was chosen because every precedence rule throws away a caller's claim silently, and the issue's rollback path forbids last-write-wins; the alternative remains available by changing the refusal to an explicit documented precedence, but that change needs a new decision record.

A refused input aborts the whole report rather than degrading one entry. This is deliberate: a caller that supplies contradictory evidence has an upstream defect, and a partial report would be quoted as if it were complete.

The orphan-evidence refusal means a caller cannot leave a physical reference in the mapping for a fault it does not currently claim. That is stricter than dropping the key, and it is the only choice that cannot quietly detach evidence from the status it supports.

coverage_report() remains a pure function over its arguments: it does not read the filesystem, so a reference that does not exist on disk is still accepted. Verifying that a cited artifact exists is out of scope for this issue and would need a separate evidence-resolution issue.
Rollback consists of reverting this commit; no schema, manifest or persisted coverage document is written by this change.
